-- RebirthService: server-authoritative rebirth system (altar, remotes, multiplier, leaderstat).
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local RebirthConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("RebirthConfig"))
local ForgeTelemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry"))
local UpgradeService: any = require(ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("UpgradeService"))

local RebirthService = {}

type State = {
	rebirths: number,
	last: number,
	altar: BasePart?,
	label: TextLabel?,
	stat: IntValue?,
}

local states: { [Player]: State } = {}
local requestRemote: RemoteEvent? = nil
local resultRemote: RemoteEvent? = nil
local started = false

local function getRemote(folder: Instance, name: string): RemoteEvent
	local existing = folder:FindFirstChild(name)
	if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		return existing
	end
	local r = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	r.Name = name
	r.Parent = folder
	return r
end

local function getCash(player: Player): IntValue?
	local ls = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if not ls then
		return nil
	end
	local c = ls:FindFirstChild("Cash")
	if c and (c:IsA("IntValue") or c:IsA("NumberValue")) then
		return c :: any
	end
	return nil
end

local function ensureState(player: Player): State
	local s = states[player]
	if not s then
		s = { rebirths = 0, last = 0, altar = nil, label = nil, stat = nil }
		states[player] = s
		player:SetAttribute("RebirthMult", RebirthConfig.multiplierFor(0))
	end
	return s
end

local function updateLabel(s: State)
	if s.label then
		s.label.Text = "REBIRTH\n$" .. tostring(RebirthConfig.costFor(s.rebirths))
			.. "\nNext: x" .. RebirthConfig.formatMultiplier(RebirthConfig.multiplierFor(s.rebirths + 1))
	end
end

local function fireResult(player: Player, ok: boolean, s: State, reason: string)
	if resultRemote then
		resultRemote:FireClient(player, ok, RebirthConfig.multiplierFor(s.rebirths), RebirthConfig.costFor(s.rebirths), reason)
	end
end

function RebirthService.tryRebirth(player: Player)
	if not player or player.Parent ~= Players then
		return
	end
	local s = ensureState(player)
	local now = os.clock()
	if now - s.last < RebirthConfig.requestCooldown then
		return
	end
	s.last = now

	local cash = getCash(player)
	local cost = RebirthConfig.costFor(s.rebirths)
	local hasAll = false
	if type(UpgradeService.hasAll) == "function" then
		local okCall, res = pcall(UpgradeService.hasAll, player)
		hasAll = okCall and res == true
	end
	local eligible = hasAll or (cash ~= nil and cash.Value >= cost)
	if not eligible or cash == nil then
		fireResult(player, false, s, "Need $" .. tostring(cost) .. " or every upgrade")
		ForgeTelemetry.count("rebirth_denied", 1)
		return
	end

	cash.Value = 0
	if type(UpgradeService.resetPlayer) == "function" then
		local okReset, err = pcall(UpgradeService.resetPlayer, player)
		if not okReset then
			warn("RebirthService: resetPlayer failed: " .. tostring(err))
		end
	end
	s.rebirths += 1
	if s.stat then
		s.stat.Value = s.rebirths
	end
	player:SetAttribute("RebirthMult", RebirthConfig.multiplierFor(s.rebirths))
	updateLabel(s)
	fireResult(player, true, s, "ok")
	ForgeTelemetry.count("rebirths", 1)
end

-- Silently sets the rebirth count (used when loading saved data): no banner, no cash reset.
function RebirthService.setRebirths(player: Player, n: number)
	if not player or player.Parent ~= Players then
		return
	end
	local count = 0
	if type(n) == "number" and n == n and n > 0 and n < math.huge then
		count = math.floor(n)
	end
	local s = ensureState(player)
	s.rebirths = count
	if s.stat then
		s.stat.Value = count
	end
	player:SetAttribute("RebirthMult", RebirthConfig.multiplierFor(count))
	updateLabel(s)
end

function RebirthService.getRebirths(player: Player): number
	local s = states[player]
	if s then
		return s.rebirths
	end
	return 0
end

function RebirthService.onPlotClaimed(player: Player, plot: any)
	local s = ensureState(player)
	if s.altar then
		s.altar:Destroy()
		s.altar, s.label = nil, nil
	end
	if type(plot) ~= "table" then
		return
	end
	local origin = plot.origin
	local cf: CFrame
	if typeof(origin) == "CFrame" then
		cf = origin
	elseif typeof(origin) == "Vector3" then
		cf = CFrame.new(origin)
	else
		return
	end
	local size = RebirthConfig.altarSize
	local altar = Instance.new("Part")
	altar.Name = "RebirthAltar_" .. player.Name
	altar.Size = size
	altar.Anchored = true
	altar.CanCollide = true
	altar.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
	altar.Color = RebirthConfig.altarColor
	altar.CFrame = cf * CFrame.new(-16, size.Y / 2, 16)

	local light = Instance.new("PointLight")
	light.Color = RebirthConfig.altarGlowColor
	light.Range = 18
	light.Brightness = 2
	light.Parent = altar

	local sparks = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
	sparks.Color = ColorSequence.new(RebirthConfig.altarGlowColor)
	sparks.Rate = 8
	sparks.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(1, 2)
	sparks.Speed = NumberRange.new(2, 4)
	sparks.Size = NumberSequence.new(0.4, 0)
	sparks.LightEmission = 1
	sparks.Parent = altar

	local bb = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	bb.Size = UDim2.fromScale(7, 4)
	bb.StudsOffset = Vector3.new(0, size.Y / 2 + 3, 0)
	bb.AlwaysOnTop = false
	bb.MaxDistance = 90
	bb.Adornee = altar
	local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	label.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	label.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	label.Font = Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy
	label.TextScaled = true
	label.TextColor3 = RebirthConfig.altarGlowColor
	label.Text = ""
	local stroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	stroke.Thickness = 3
	stroke.Color = Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38)
	stroke.Parent = label
	label.Parent = bb
	bb.Parent = altar

	local prompt = Instance.new("ProximityPrompt")
	prompt.ActionText = "Rebirth"
	prompt.ObjectText = "Golden Altar"
	prompt.HoldDuration = 0.5
	prompt.MaxActivationDistance = 10
	prompt.RequiresLineOfSight = false
	prompt.Triggered:Connect(function(who: Player)
		if who == player then
			RebirthService.tryRebirth(player)
		end
	end)
	prompt.Parent = altar

	s.altar, s.label = altar, label
	updateLabel(s)
	altar.Parent = Workspace
end

function RebirthService.onPlotReleased(player: Player)
	local s = states[player]
	if s and s.altar then
		s.altar:Destroy()
		s.altar, s.label = nil, nil
	end
end

local function setupPlayer(player: Player)
	local s = ensureState(player)
	task.spawn(function()
		local ls = player:WaitForChild("leaderstats", 10)
		if not ls then
			local f = Instance.new("Folder")
			f.Name = "leaderstats"
			f.Parent = player
			ls = f
		end
		if player.Parent ~= Players or s.stat then
			return
		end
		local stat = ls:FindFirstChild("Rebirths")
		if not (stat and stat:IsA("IntValue")) then
			stat = Instance.new("IntValue")
			stat.Name = "Rebirths"
			stat.Value = s.rebirths
			stat.Parent = ls
		else
			stat.Value = s.rebirths
		end
		s.stat = stat :: IntValue
	end)
end

local function removePlayer(player: Player)
	RebirthService.onPlotReleased(player)
	states[player] = nil
end

function RebirthService.init()
	if started then
		return
	end
	started = true
	local folder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("Remotes")
	if not folder then
		folder = Instance.new("Folder")
		folder.Name = "Remotes"
		folder.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	end
	requestRemote = getRemote(folder, "RebirthRequest")
	resultRemote = getRemote(folder, "RebirthResult")
	if requestRemote then
		requestRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player)
			RebirthService.tryRebirth(player)
		end)
	end
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(setupPlayer)
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(removePlayer)
	for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
		setupPlayer(p)
	end
end

return RebirthService

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## Fixing and debugging
- A "sync" StudioError about not being able to serve a path is an infrastructure or environment failure, not a code bug. Do not change game code in response. Retry the step.
- If the critic says a code path was never exercised in the playtest, fix the pacing or setup so the path actually runs (e.g. cheaper first purchase) instead of only adding more code.
- When the spec changes the flow (e.g. from auto-assign to claim), rewrite the entry script (Game.server) to require and wire the new modules, and delete the old flow's logic (slots, teleport on join). Updating only the new modules leaves the old behaviour running.
- After a redesign, check that every module is required by the entry script and that its init function is called. Unwired modules never run, and their counters never fire.
